conflicts.issue: Lymphoma of the nasopharynx, adenoid, tonsil or Waldeyer ring is Group II (ICCC-2017 IIa, IIb2, IIb3, IIc at every site). Nasopharyngeal lymphomas are 15% of head and neck lymphomas; diffuse large B-cell and NK/T-cell lymphoma are named.
Rhabdomyosarcoma (IXa) and extraosseous Ewing sarcoma (IXd2) of the pharynx are Group IX at every site. The ICCR carcinoma dataset excludes sarcomas.
Chordoma of the clivus reaches the nasopharynx; ICCC-2017 places 9370/3 in VIIId2 at every site. Referred with the site recaptured.

Craniopharyngioma (IIIe2) and ectopic pituitary adenoma or pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (IIIe1) are Group III at every site, behaviours 0, 1 and 3, so a benign ectopic pituitary adenoma of the nasopharynx is registrable in Group III.

Myoepithelial carcinoma (8982/3), malignant mixed tumour (8940/3) and sialoblastoma (8974) are XIIa4 at every site. A salivary gland-type myoepithelial carcinoma of the nasopharynx or oropharynx is Group XII by ICCC-2017; the salivary part decides how the salivary screens route it.

Nasopharyngeal dermoid (9084/0) is benign and not registrable; a teratoma with malignant transformation (9084/3) at C11 is Xb2. Hairy polyp, which Badoual calls a form of teratoma, is benign and has no ICD-O-3.2 term.

Within Group XI: these valid /3 codes have no ICCC-2017 range at C11 (XIc's ranges stop short of them; XIf10 excludes C11). 8085/8086 are not offered at C11; 8240/8249 are picker entries; 8941 and 8147 are salivary types the salivary part names. The subgroup computation must return XIc for them at C11.

Within Group XI: a tumour over the nasopharynx and oropharynx with no stated origin is C14.8 (XIf10), and a neck deposit with no primary is C80.9 (XIf11). The nasopharyngeal codes then fall in XIf10 or XIf11, not XIc.
